text:
Mitch Marner's second season in Vegas reads like a passer's diary: 23 assists, 3 goals, 26 points in 20 games. He's on a four-game point streak, RotoBaller had his home point streak at 10 games, and he even scored shorthanded on a breakaway against Buffalo.

The goals are the odd part. He has 3 on 5.6 expected goals (the quality of his chances), shooting 6.2% when our range for a player like him runs from about 11% to 15%. The looks are there and the finish isn't, which is the kind of gap that usually closes on its own.

His game hasn't changed. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 62% of his exits leaving the zone with possession last season and 8.2 primary shot assists per 60, 83rd percentile among forwards. Evolving-Hockey had him 16th of 401 forwards at 2.9 wins above replacement. He isn't fast by the tracking numbers (27th percentile in top speed); he wins with his hands and his head. Watch whether the goals start to match the chances, because the assists already do.
headline: Marner is setting the table, not finishing
